newsitem.title: USA: Sotheby's higher revs helped boost net.
newsitem.headline: Sotheby's higher revs helped boost net.

text.p: Sotheby's Holdings Inc said Tuesday that higher revenues in all of its major businesses helped boost net income before charges during the first half of the year to its highest level in seven years.
"The growth in first half net income was due to a 12 percent increase in revenues, which totaled $185.1 million compared to $165.4 million during the same period in 1996," it said in a statement.
Sotheby's Holdings, the parent company of the auction house Sothey's, reported a net income of $0.51 per share for the second quarter and $0.40 for the first half of the year.
In 1996, it had $0.50 per share for the second quarter and $0.36 for the first half.
"The increase in earnings was driven by higher profits in all of our major businesses: auction and related activities, art-related financing and real estate," it said.
The operating share figure for the second quarter was $0.55 against $0.50 for the same period a year ago. For the first six months of the year, it reported $0.46 a share against $0.36.
